shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures fell on Thursday, as a slump in Tokyo equities, weaker Chinese rubber imports, and profit-taking after a recent rally weighed on sentiment.($1 = 157.8400 yen)($1 = 6.6926 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures fell on Thursday, as a slump in Tokyo equities, weaker Chinese rubber imports, and profit-taking after a recent rally weighed on sentiment.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for March delivery
was down 6.4 yen, or 1.41%, at 447 yen ($2.83) per kg as of 0055 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
slumped 575 yuan, or 2.84%, to 19,640 yuan ($2,934.58) per metric ton
The most active November butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) fell 425 yuan, or 2.64%, to 15,675 yuan per metric ton
Rubber prices may be tracking broader risk sentiment and profit-taking following a recent run-up, a Singapore-based trader said
With prices now near support levels, short positions could face a squeeze given the continued tightness in raw material supply, the trader said
share average slumped in early trading on Thursday, with tech stocks hit hard after hot US inflation figures sparked fears of higher interest rates
China imported 588,000 tons of natural and synthetic rubber in September, down 20.8% from 742,000 tons a year earlier, the General Administration of Customs of China said on Wednesday
Imports totaled 5.68 million tons in the first nine months of the year, down 7.1% from 6.11 million tons in the same period last year
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) last traded at 247.7 US cents per kg, down 2.7%
